takeaway: Dukes': A confined to the wall, B through the wall, C1 nodes not including the apical node, C2 including the apical node, D distant metastasis. Through the wall plus an apical node and no metastasis is C2.

question.text: After a right hemicolectomy, the tumour invades through the bowel wall into adjacent structures and the apical node is involved. No metastasis on CT. Which Dukes' stage?

lines.text: Dr Cuthbert Dukes described this staging back in 1932.
Stage A is a tumour confined to the bowel wall. Stage B is a tumour penetrating the wall.
Our tumour is through the wall into adjacent structures, so it is at least stage B.
Stage C is about nodes. C one means nodes, but not the apical node.
C two means lymph node involvement including the apical node, the top bead on the ladder.
lines.say: C two means lymph node involvement including the apical node, the top bead on the ladder. (laugh)

lines.text: Stage D needs distant metastasis, and the CT showed none.
So the answer is Dukes stage C two.
